headers.comment: Security headers on every response (defense-in-depth; the app has no HTML-injection sink today, this guards against future drift). CSP notes: script/style need 'unsafe-inline' because index.html carries the no-flash theme script and React sets inline style attributes (RangeSlider/StatsPage bars) — external script origins are still locked down, which is the main win. connect-src covers Firestore/Auth/Storage (*.googleapis.com incl. long-polling), the auth helper (*.google.com) and Sentry ingest; frame-src covers the Google sign-in popup/iframe (authDomain on firebaseapp.com + accounts.google.com); img-src allows the app's own assets, object-URL photo previews (blob:), Storage downloads and Google avatars. If a legit origin ever gets blocked, loosen the single directive — or drop this block wholesale to roll back.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' https://*.googleapis.com https://*.google.com https://*.ingest.de.sentry.io https://*.ingest.sentry.io; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com https://lh3.googleusercontent.com; frame-src https://*.firebaseapp.com https://accounts.google.com; worker-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'

headers.comment: version.json, index.html and sw.js must never be cached. A stale version.json/index.html would hide a new build from a long-open tab; a stale sw.js would pin an old service worker (Firebase Hosting's default 1h cache would otherwise delay every SW update by up to an hour).
Hashed build assets are content-addressed, so they can be cached forever.
